stories.title: Moldovan parliament backs energy state of emergency after power line knocked out of service
stories.summary: Moldova's parliament approved a 60-day energy state of emergency after Russian strikes on neighboring Ukraine disabled a power line that supplies most of Moldova's electricity.

stories.title: Pope Leo laments that Iran war 'getting worse and worse'
stories.summary: Pope Leo voiced concern over the escalating Iran war, calling for a ceasefire. His remarks came amid reports that the United States is planning to deploy thousands of additional soldiers to the Middle East.

stories.title: Venezuelan man sues US over deportation to El Salvadoran prison
stories.summary: A Venezuelan man filed a lawsuit seeking at least $1.3 million in damages against the U.S. government, alleging he was wrongfully identified as a gang member and deported to a prison in El Salvador in violation of a U.S. court order.

stories.title: Two dead in school shooting in western Mexico; teenager arrested
stories.summary: A 15-year-old boy was arrested after allegedly shooting and killing two female staff members, including a teacher, at a private school in the western Mexican state of Michoacán, according to local authorities.

stories.title: Colombia seeks arrest of rebel leaders over 2025 assassination of senator
stories.summary: Colombia's attorney general issued arrest warrants for the top leaders of the Segunda Marquetalia rebel group in connection with the 2025 assassination of senator and presidential hopeful Miguel Uribe.

stories.title: Iran says 'non-hostile' ships can transit Strait of Hormuz, FT reports
stories.summary: Iran informed International Maritime Organization member states that non-hostile vessels may transit the Strait of Hormuz if they coordinate with Iranian authorities, according to a letter reported by the Financial Times.

stories.title: Danish left-wing bloc leads election, lacks majority, exit polls show
stories.summary: Exit polls from Denmark's election showed the left-wing bloc leading but neither the left nor the right expected to secure a majority of parliamentary seats.

stories.title: French tycoon Bollore denies political war against public broadcaster
stories.summary: French media tycoon Vincent Bolloré testified before lawmakers in Paris, denying accusations that his conservative media empire is waging a political war against public broadcasting. He called himself a scapegoat for a hostile elite.

stories.title: Top US official does not rule out resuming underground nuclear weapons tests
stories.summary: A senior U.S. State Department official said Washington is still assessing how to implement President Trump's order to resume nuclear weapons testing and did not rule out full-scale underground explosive tests.

stories.title: Trump says Iran made a major energy-related gift to the US
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated that Iran had made a major energy-related concession to the United States, calling it a positive development, but provided no specific details.

stories.title: Gulf warnings and fears of miscalculation preceded Trump’s pause in Iran showdown
stories.summary: Gulf states warned the U.S. that its confrontation with Iran was entering a more dangerous phase, with regional officials fearing Washington had underestimated Tehran's willingness to escalate, according to regional sources. The warnings preceded Trump's abrupt pause in the standoff.

stories.title: Ghana's president, in New York, says US 'normalising' erasure of Black history
stories.summary: Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama, speaking in New York, criticized the U.S. administration for what he described as normalizing the erasure of Black history and warned such policies could have broader international consequences.

stories.title: Venezuela opposition leader Maria Corina Machado pushes for energy investment security, transparency
stories.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, speaking in Houston, welcomed early interest in Venezuela's oil sector but called for greater transparency, contract security, and a new oil law to boost crude and gas production.

stories.title: US expected to send thousands more soldiers to Middle East, sources say
stories.summary: The Pentagon is expected to deploy thousands of soldiers from the U.S. Army's 82nd Airborne Division to the Middle East, adding to a significant military buildup even as President Trump discusses a possible deal with Tehran to end the conflict.

stories.title: Three US and Czech citizens detained over arson attack on Czech arms producer
stories.summary: Czech police detained three individuals — holding U.S. and Czech citizenship — in connection with an arson attack on a Czech arms producer. Authorities did not specify the exact nationalities of the detainees.

stories.title: ​Cowardly bully: On Donald Trump and the Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump faces criticism over the ongoing war involving Iran, with calls for him to end hostilities and pressure Israel to cease its operations against Iran.

stories.title: Several injured as Karachi-bound Tezgam Express derails near Punjab’s Lodhran: official
stories.summary: The Karachi-bound Tezgam Express derailed near Lodhran in Punjab, Pakistan, on Tuesday night. At least 17 people received first aid on site, while eight others were hospitalized. Pakistan Railways reported no fatalities and said a high-level inquiry had been ordered.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Trump says Iran gave U.S. 'very big present' related to oil and gas
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated on Tuesday that negotiations with Iran to end the Middle East war were actively underway. He claimed Tehran was eager to reach a deal and had offered the U.S. a significant concession related to oil and gas.

stories.title: Clerics from Pakistan, Afghanistan appeal to authorities to extend pause in fighting till Eidul Azha
stories.summary: A group of clerics from Pakistan and Afghanistan called on authorities in both countries to extend the pause in hostilities, originally announced for Eidul Fitr, through Eidul Azha. Pakistan's government had initially declared the pause on March 18 at the request of Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Turkey.

stories.title: Modi, Dissanayake discuss ‘energy cooperation’ over telephone call
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake spoke by telephone to discuss energy cooperation. The two leaders also addressed the ongoing war in West Asia and its impact on global supply chains.

stories.title: War Diary Day 25: Pause holds but conflict’s underlying dynamics point to widening of scope
stories.summary: On day 25 of the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, Israeli strikes continued targeting energy and military infrastructure in Isfahan, Khorramshahr, and Tehran. President Trump's five-day pause on strikes against Iranian energy facilities provided limited respite, with the conflict's scope continuing to widen.

stories.title: Germany detains two Russian agents spying on supplier of drones for Ukraine
stories.summary: German federal prosecutors detained a Romanian woman and a Ukrainian man on suspicion of spying for a Russian intelligence service. The pair allegedly gathered information and filmed a person involved in supplying drones and drone components to Ukraine.

stories.title: China is mapping the ocean floor as it prepares for submarine warfare with the U.S.
stories.summary: China is deploying research vessels to systematically map the ocean floor, navigating in tight survey lines to gather detailed underwater terrain data. The effort is linked to preparations for potential submarine warfare with the United States.

stories.title: Lviv drone strike: 26 victims hospitalized
stories.summary: Twenty-six people injured during a Russian drone attack on the western Ukrainian city of Lviv on March 24 remain hospitalized. The strike was part of Russia's broader aerial campaign against Ukrainian cities.

stories.title: Russia fires nearly 400 drones at Ukraine with signs its spring offensive has started
stories.summary: Russia launched nearly 400 drones at Ukraine in a major escalation that may signal the start of a long-anticipated spring ground offensive. Moscow's forces intensified efforts to breach Ukrainian front-line defenses across the front.

stories.title: Zelensky on massive attack: Russia not seeking to end war, more pressure needed
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Russia's massive ongoing drone attacks, which have injured more than 40 people including five children, demonstrate that Moscow is not seeking to end the war. He called for increased pressure on Russia.

stories.title: Former IRGC commander Mohhammad Baqer Zolqadr named Iran’s new security chief
stories.summary: Former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander Mohammad Baqer Zolqadr has been appointed Iran's new security chief. Zolqadr, who served as secretary of the Expediency Discernment Council, replaces Ali Larijani in the role.

stories.title: Strikes hit Iran, Tehran targets Israel and Gulf states amid mixed signals over talks to end war
stories.summary: Strikes continued to hit targets in Iran while Tehran launched attacks against Israel and Gulf states, amid conflicting signals over potential peace talks. Uncertainty persists over who in Iran's government holds the authority or willingness to negotiate, especially after Israel killed several senior leaders.

stories.title: No real progress toward peace from Russia yet – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said there has been no real movement toward peace from Russia, citing information from his negotiation team that returned from talks in the United States.

stories.title: Feds charge Chicago man with threatening to ‘shoot up a synagogue’ after Khamenei’s killing
stories.summary: Federal authorities charged Timothy Holmes, 31, of Chicago with threatening to shoot up a synagogue following the killing of Iranian Supreme Leader Khamenei. Holmes allegedly posted antisemitic comments online in response to posts about Israel.

stories.title: India an ‘essential’ U.S. partner in Indo-Pacific, its rise is good for American interests, says top Pentagon official
stories.summary: U.S. Assistant Secretary of Defense Elbridge Colby described India as an essential American partner in the Indo-Pacific, stating that India's rise serves U.S. interests. He acknowledged that the two nations can manage their differences, though he made no reference to the Quad alliance.

stories.title: Iran claims Israel, US, attacked near nuclear power plant, no technical damage or casualties
stories.summary: Iran reported that an attack by Israel and the United States struck near a nuclear power plant. Iranian authorities said initial assessments indicated no technical damage to the facility and no casualties.

stories.title: Ukraine calls for cultural sanctions after Russian strike damages UNESCO heritage site in Lviv
stories.summary: Ukraine called for cultural sanctions against Russia after a Russian strike damaged a UNESCO World Heritage site in the central part of Lviv. Ukrainian officials described the attack as a cultural crime and an act of barbarism.

stories.title: Nepal’s political shift opens a strategic window for India
stories.summary: A recent political transition in Nepal has created a potential strategic opening for India. Analysts suggest the new Nepali government presents an opportunity for both countries to develop a forward-looking bilateral relationship.

stories.title: Sindh minister says govt contemplating smart lockdown as fuel conservation measure
stories.summary: Sindh Local Government Minister Nasir Hussain Shah announced that Pakistan's Sindh province is considering a smart lockdown as a fuel conservation measure amid the global oil crisis linked to the U.S.-Israel war on Iran. The provincial government has already cut official vehicle fuel allowances by 60 percent.

stories.title: Europe within Iran missile range, but experts question real strike capability
stories.summary: Security experts note that Iran possesses missiles capable of reaching parts of Europe but question the country's actual strike capability at that range. Analysts warn Iran could pursue indirect retaliation through cyber sabotage, arson, and proxy attacks on soft targets including energy infrastructure and Jewish sites.

stories.title: Russian drone attack damages energy facilities in Ternopil region, 70,000 left without power
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack struck energy facilities in Ukraine's Ternopil region, leaving approximately 70,000 people without power. Fires at the damaged energy infrastructure and an administrative building have since been extinguished.

stories.title: Trump okayed op after Netanyahu argued for killing of Khamenei
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly urged President Donald Trump to approve the U.S.-Israel strike on Iran hours before it was launched. Netanyahu cited intelligence suggesting Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei was vulnerable and alleged an Iranian plot to assassinate Trump.

stories.title: Long lines, unpaid TSA workers: Experts say US air travel system in crisis
stories.summary: Experts warn the U.S. air travel system is in crisis as TSA workers face unpaid wages during a government shutdown. Staffing shortages at major airports have led to long security lines and widespread disruptions for travelers.

stories.title: AJK PM condemns sentencing of Kashmiri leader Asiya Andrabi, her associates by Indian court
stories.summary: Azad Jammu and Kashmir Prime Minister Raja Faisal Mumtaz Rathore condemned the sentencing of Kashmiri leader Asiya Andrabi to life imprisonment by an Indian NIA special court in New Delhi. Her associates Fehmida Sofi and Nahida Nasreen received 30-year sentences. Rathore called the verdicts political coercion aimed at silencing dissent.

stories.title: France's Macron urges Iranian president to end attacks
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron spoke with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and urged him to halt attacks against countries in the region. Macron also called for the preservation of energy and civilian infrastructure and the restoration of freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Building collapses after Iranian missile strike on Israel
stories.summary: A building in Bnei Brak, near Tel Aviv, collapsed after being struck by an Iranian missile, according to Israeli authorities. The incident occurred amid an escalating exchange of fire between Iran and Israel.

stories.title: Trump claims US has achieved ‘regime change’, ‘received present’ from Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that the United States had achieved regime change in Iran, claiming the country had "received a present" from Iran. No further details on the claim were immediately provided.

stories.title: Iraq to summon US, Iran envoys over deadly attacks: PM’s office
stories.summary: The Iraqi Prime Minister's office announced plans to summon the U.S. and Iranian ambassadors and deliver formal notes of protest over deadly attacks on Iraqi territory. The strikes are tied to the ongoing U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Pakistan’s petrol cargoes for March and April ‘largely secured’: finance ministry
stories.summary: Pakistan's finance ministry said petrol cargoes for March and April have been largely secured, with additional shipments planned to strengthen supply buffers. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb chaired a committee meeting to review the energy supply situation amid evolving geopolitical conditions and global oil market disruptions.

stories.title: NASA to spend $20bn on moon base, nuclear-powered Mars spacecraft
stories.summary: NASA plans to allocate $20 billion toward constructing a lunar base and increasing robotic missions to the Moon. The agency also intends to launch a nuclear-powered spacecraft called Space Reactor 1 Freedom for Mars exploration.

stories.title: Sybiha urges UNESCO to respond to Russian strike on central Lviv
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha urged UNESCO Director-General Khaled El-Enany to respond decisively to a Russian strike on central Lviv. The targeted area is designated a UNESCO World Heritage site.

stories.title: Iranian missiles cause injuries and major damage across Israel
stories.summary: Iran launched a wave of missiles targeting areas across Israel, causing injuries and significant damage. Iran released video footage showing the missile launches.

stories.title: Iranian missile intercepted above Lebanon, shrapnel falls on towns in Beirut
stories.summary: Shrapnel from an intercepted Iranian missile fell on several towns north of Beirut, Lebanon, causing light injuries. The Lebanese news agency reported the debris resulted from the interception of the missile over Lebanese territory.

stories.title: Trump insists Iran regime change already happened, claims Iranians want a deal 'very badly'
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that negotiations with Iran are underway but declined to provide details. He claimed Iranians want a deal "very badly" and asserted that regime change in Iran had already occurred.

stories.title: Sydney teenager charged with terror offences after allegedly posting threats of extremist violence
stories.summary: New South Wales police in Sydney charged a 16-year-old boy with multiple terrorism offences after he allegedly posted threats of extremist violence online. The Australian Joint Counter Terrorism Team had initially arrested the teenager in December on weapons offences following reports of violent threats.

stories.title: US air superiority over Iran hobbled by lower-altitude threats, experts say
stories.summary: Military experts say the United States faces challenges to its air superiority over Iran due to lower-altitude threats. The assessment comes amid ongoing hostilities, with Iranian missile attacks visible over locations including Netanya, Israel.

stories.title: Ukraine makes significant efforts to conduct search operations even during war – Alfyorov
stories.summary: Ukrainian official Alfyorov stated that Ukraine is devoting significant financial, organizational, and security resources to search and exhumation operations despite the ongoing war. The operations are being conducted in accordance with agreements with Poland.

stories.title: Half-asleep, sheltering underground: Tel Aviv residents seek normalcy under rocket fire
stories.summary: Residents of Tel Aviv are sheltering underground in tent-city shelters, empty offices, and shopping malls amid ongoing Iranian rocket fire. Civilians are contending with fatigue and fear while attempting to maintain daily routines during the conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Danish PM's left bloc leads election, but no majority
stories.summary: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's left bloc took an early lead in Tuesday's general election but failed to secure a majority, according to exit polls. Frederiksen's Social Democrats posted their weakest result in 125 years.

stories.title: Has Iran brought down an ‘unkillable’ US F-35 jet?
stories.summary: Iran claims it struck a U.S. F-35 fighter jet and released footage purporting to show the incident. The claim raises questions about the vulnerability of the advanced stealth aircraft.

stories.title: Army C2 to see more budget line consolidation in FY27, says service undersecretary
stories.summary: The U.S. Army plans further consolidation of command-and-control budget lines in its fiscal year 2027 request, according to the service's undersecretary. In the FY26 budget, Congress approved consolidating 13 lines related to electronic warfare, counter-drone systems, and unmanned aerial systems.

stories.title: Pakistan stands ‘ready, honoured’ to host US-Iran talks, says PM Shehbaz
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced that Pakistan stands "ready and honoured" to host negotiations between the United States and Iran. Sharif expressed support for dialogue aimed at ending the war in the Middle East and achieving a comprehensive settlement.

stories.title: AIPAC pushes back after 2028 Democratic presidential hopefuls reject it
stories.summary: Several leading Democratic lawmakers positioning for the 2028 U.S. presidential race have refused support from the pro-Israel lobby group AIPAC. AIPAC has pushed back against the rejections, which reflect growing tensions within the Democratic Party over U.S.-Israel relations.

stories.title: Supreme Court justices lean towards Trump in asylum-processing case
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court appeared likely to side with the Trump administration in a case involving its authority to turn away asylum seekers at the U.S.-Mexico border. The dispute centers on a "metering" policy that limits processing when border crossings are deemed overburdened.

stories.title: Iranian missile intercepted over Lebanon in first since war
stories.summary: Shrapnel from an intercepted Iranian missile struck buildings north of Beirut, Lebanon, marking the first such interception over Lebanese territory since the war began. Unverified reports suggest a US asset may also have been affected.

stories.title: Canadian woman held with daughter by ICE warns all immigrants to ‘lie low’
stories.summary: Tania Warner, a Canadian woman, says she and her seven-year-old daughter have been detained by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement despite possessing documents showing legal status. Warner has urged other immigrants to avoid checkpoints and keep a low profile during the Trump presidency.

stories.title: Nearly 1,000 drones in one day: Ukrainian Air Force reports one of largest Russian attacks on Ukraine
stories.summary: On March 24, Russia launched more than 550 strike drones against Ukraine during daytime hours, with the total over 24 hours reaching nearly 1,000. The Ukrainian Air Force reported the barrage included Shahed, Gerber, and other drone types, making it one of the largest such attacks of the war.

stories.title: Russia hits Ukraine with rare daytime barrage as new offensive begins
stories.summary: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Kyiv faces a shortage of interceptor missiles as Russia carried out a rare daytime barrage coinciding with a new offensive. Zelenskyy noted that Washington's attention is currently focused on its military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Russia fires nearly 1,000 drones at Ukraine in 24 hours, killing at least eight
stories.summary: Russia launched nearly 1,000 drones at Ukraine within 24 hours, killing at least eight people in one of its largest-ever daytime attacks. A UNESCO heritage site in Lviv was damaged. President Zelenskyy condemned Moscow's actions and said Russia shows no intention of ending the war.

stories.title: Second set of rare gorilla twins born in DR Congo reserve Goma, DR Congo
stories.summary: An endangered mountain gorilla gave birth to a rare set of twins in Virunga National Park in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, near Goma. It is the second recorded set of gorilla twins born in the reserve, whose biodiversity has been threatened by ongoing regional conflicts.

stories.title: US to deploy 3,000 82nd Airborne Division troops to Middle East to support Iran war - WSJ
stories.summary: The US military has ordered approximately 3,000 troops from the 82nd Airborne Division to deploy to the Middle East in support of operations related to the Iran conflict, according to the Wall Street Journal. Officials said the order does not confirm a decision by President Trump to send ground forces into Iran.

stories.title: Woman killed, 2 injured in Hezbollah rocket attack on northern Israel
stories.summary: A woman was killed and two others were injured in a Hezbollah rocket attack on northern Israel. Separately, Iranian missile impacts were reported in Safed, lightly wounding two people. The IDF said it killed an Iranian Revolutionary Guard official in a strike on Beirut and five Hezbollah operatives in south Lebanon.

stories.title: US, Israel attacked vicinity of Bushehr nuclear plant, Iran says
stories.summary: Iran's Atomic Energy Organisation reported that the US and Israel attacked the vicinity of the Bushehr nuclear power plant on Tuesday evening local time. Initial assessments indicated the strike caused no technical damage to the facility and no human casualties.

stories.title: Russian attack on Lviv: Injury toll rises to 22
stories.summary: Following a Russian drone strike on Lviv on March 24, the number of people injured in the city rose to at least 17, with the overall toll reaching 22. The attack targeted areas in the western Ukrainian city.

stories.title: Pakistan’s prime minister says his nation is ready to facilitate talks to end Iran war
stories.summary: Pakistan's Prime Minister stated that his country is prepared to facilitate negotiations aimed at ending the conflict between the US and Iran. Pakistan joins other nations pushing diplomatically for talks after President Trump indicated that negotiations between Washington and Tehran were underway.

stories.title: Russia’s spring offensive is failing. It launches record drone attack to make sure nobody noticed
stories.summary: Russia launched a record number of drones against Ukraine as part of a large-scale attack, coinciding with what analysts describe as a failing spring ground offensive. President Trump subsequently claimed that peace was near.

stories.title: ‘If Iran keeps its uranium, everything was for nothing’: Experts, officials react to Trump's pause
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced a five-day halt in US strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure after describing ongoing talks as productive. Experts and officials are debating whether the pause eases military pressure on Iran prematurely, particularly regarding its uranium enrichment program.

stories.title: Saudi leader said to be pushing Trump to continue war in Iran, New York Times reports
stories.summary: The New York Times reported that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has been urging President Trump to continue the military campaign against Iran. The Saudi leader reportedly argued that the US-Israeli operation represents a historic opportunity to reshape the Middle East.

stories.title: Russian forces strike center of Zhytomyr, injuring 12-year-old child
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the center of Zhytomyr, Ukraine, on March 24, injuring a 12-year-old girl. The attack targeted the city center of the regional capital located west of Kyiv.

stories.title: French municipal vote: What do results mean for 2027 ballot?
stories.summary: France's National Rally party underperformed expectations in recent municipal elections. However, analysts caution that mainstream parties should not be complacent, as the results may not reliably predict outcomes in the 2027 presidential race.

stories.title: Russian nighttime attacks on Poltava leave more than 40 buildings damaged
stories.summary: A nighttime Russian attack on the Ukrainian city of Poltava damaged more than 40 buildings, including residential homes and social infrastructure facilities.

stories.title: US legislative failures are giving China a strategic edge, Anduril exec says
stories.summary: Anduril co-founder told U.S. lawmakers that congressional dysfunction in passing legislation is providing China a strategic advantage in the competition for military and technological supremacy.

stories.title: The first Russian officer to speak out in detail about the torture of Ukrainian POWs has now spent three years in the U.S. Here’s his story.
stories.summary: Konstantin Efremov, a Russian military officer from North Ossetia, deployed during Moscow's 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, left the military three months later and relocated to the United States. He publicly detailed accounts of Russian troops torturing Ukrainian prisoners of war, abusing civilians, and mistreating fellow soldiers who refused to fight.

stories.title: 'We need a more European NATO': Rasmussen warns the US is 'turning its back on Europe'
stories.summary: Former NATO Secretary General Anders Fogh Rasmussen warned that the United States is withdrawing from its commitments to European defense. He called for a more European-oriented NATO, arguing that Europe must address its longstanding dependency on external security guarantees.

stories.title: Sudan's RSF says captured strategic town on Ethiopia border
stories.summary: Sudan's Rapid Support Forces (RSF) claimed to have captured Kurmuk, a strategically important border town near Ethiopia, following intense fighting with the Sudanese Armed Forces. The seizure threatens vital supply and transit routes between Sudan and Ethiopia.

stories.title: Why Pakistan may be the 'perfect' mediator between Iran and US
stories.summary: Pakistan is reportedly positioning itself as a mediator between Iran and the United States, leveraging its diplomatic relationships with Washington, Tehran, and Gulf states amid the ongoing U.S.-Israeli military campaign.

stories.title: US says they’re talking, Iran says they’re not. Who’s telling the truth?
stories.summary: The United States and Iran have offered contradictory statements about whether nuclear or diplomatic negotiations are underway. Critics suggest the Trump administration's claims of ongoing talks may be intended to stabilize financial markets.

stories.title: Russian drone attack on Ivano-Frankivsk leaves two killed and four injured
stories.summary: A Russian drone strike on the western Ukrainian city of Ivano-Frankivsk killed two people and injured four others, including a six-year-old child.

stories.title: EU Delays Proposal to Permanently Ban Russian Oil
stories.summary: The European Commission has postponed its proposal to permanently ban Russian oil imports, with no new date announced. EU Commission energy spokeswoman Anna-Kaisa Itkonen said Brussels remains committed to presenting the proposal.

stories.title: ADB announces support package for developing member states hit by Middle East conflict
stories.summary: The Asian Development Bank announced a financial support package for developing member countries affected by the Middle East conflict. ADB President Masato Kanda said the assistance would include fast-disbursing budget support and trade and supply chain finance to help secure imports of essential goods, including oil.

stories.title: How Russia’s school history lessons are reframing Stalin, Gorbachev, and the war in Ukraine
stories.summary: Since 2023, Russian high schools have used a single standardized history textbook led by Putin aide Vladimir Medinsky, with the stated goal of fostering patriotism. Beginning in September 2026, all Russian schools from fifth grade onward will adopt the same unified textbook series.

stories.title: Russian drone attack on Vinnytsia region leaves one killed and 11 others injured
stories.summary: A Russian drone strike on Ukraine's Vinnytsia region killed one person and injured 11 others.

stories.title: Four Things the Gulf States Will Expect From the U.S. After the Iran War
stories.summary: Gulf states that host U.S. military forces are signaling they expect a more reciprocal partnership with Washington in the aftermath of conflict with Iran, rather than serving solely as military staging platforms.

stories.title: Crisis-Struck Philippines Reportedly Buys Russian Oil For First Time in 5 Years
stories.summary: Ship tracking data indicates the Philippines received Russian oil for the first time in five years, with the Sierra Leone-flagged tanker Sara Sky arriving at the Limay anchorage in Manila Bay.

stories.title: Egypt’s Mohamed Salah to leave Liverpool at end of season after 9-year stay
stories.summary: Egyptian forward Mohamed Salah is set to depart Liverpool after nine seasons with the Premier League club. He has been linked with a potential move to Saudi Arabia's Pro League.

stories.title: Drone attack on Lviv: Injury toll rises to 13
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack on the western Ukrainian city of Lviv injured at least 13 people. Authorities reported the rising casualty toll as rescue operations continued.

stories.title: Blackouts, Food Shortages, and Water Scarcity
stories.summary: Cuba is facing severe blackouts, food shortages, and water scarcity amid a halt in oil shipments. The lack of fuel deliveries has deepened the country's humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: Talks or theatre? Claims of peace talks to end Iran war collide with denials
stories.summary: Conflicting claims have emerged over whether diplomatic talks to end the conflict involving Iran are under way. President Trump suggested major progress, but the White House downplayed the remarks, and Iran denied any negotiations. Pakistan has been named as a possible venue, while Israel announced plans to push into southern Lebanon up to the Litani River against Hezbollah.

stories.title: What impact is the war on Iran having on Israel?
stories.summary: Iranian missiles struck Israeli territory as the ongoing conflict between the two countries continued. The war has contributed to deepening global economic disruption.

stories.title: Russia’s record attack of war kills newborn and her father at maternity hospital in Ivano-Frankivsk. Baby was days old
stories.summary: During Russia's largest drone attack of the full-scale war on March 23–24, strikes hit a maternity hospital in the western Ukrainian city of Ivano-Frankivsk. A newborn baby and her father were killed in the assault.

stories.title: Afghanistan releases American national Dennis Coyle after more than year
stories.summary: The Taliban government in Afghanistan released American national Dennis Coyle after more than a year of detention. Coyle had been held since January 2025 on unspecified allegations; Afghan authorities never publicly disclosed which laws he was accused of violating.

stories.title: Why is Trump asking for Europe’s help in war on Iran?
stories.summary: Former French Ambassador to the United States Gérard Araud argued that European nations are justified in declining involvement in the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran. The debate centers on why the Trump administration has sought European participation in the conflict.

stories.title: Aid flotilla vessel arrives in Cuba amid US-driven energy crisis
stories.summary: An aid flotilla vessel arrived in Cuba as the island faces an energy crisis linked to U.S. restrictions. Activists described the delivery as a symbolic gesture of solidarity intended to highlight the impact of the U.S. energy blockade on Cuban civilians.

stories.title: Tehran 24 March 2026 #1
stories.summary: Mohammad Baqer Zolqhadr was appointed secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council on March 24, 2026, in Tehran.

stories.title: Lebanon 24 March 2026 #2
stories.summary: Lebanon's foreign minister on March 24, 2026, ordered the withdrawal of agrément for designated Iranian Ambassador Mohammad Reza Shibani. Shibani was declared persona non grata and instructed to leave Lebanese territory no later than March 29, 2026.

stories.title: Lebanon 24 March 2026 #1
stories.summary: On March 24, 2026, Israel's defense minister declared that the IDF would continue full-force operations in southern Lebanon against Hezbollah. He stated that hundreds of thousands of displaced southern Lebanese residents would not be permitted to return south of the Litani River until northern Israel's security was ensured.

stories.title: Israel 24 March 2026 #1
stories.summary: Israel's defense minister on March 24, 2026, announced that the IDF would maintain full-force operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon. He stated residents of southern Lebanon who evacuated northward would not return south of the Litani River until Israeli security in the north was guaranteed.

stories.title: Denmark outspends everyone on Ukraine. I walked the streets to find out why.
stories.summary: Denmark leads the world in per-capita support for Ukraine. As Danes headed to the polls on March 24, Ukraine was largely absent as a campaign issue, with approximately 70% of the population already backing the country's high level of aid.

stories.title: Israel says will take 'control' of security zone in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel announced it would take control of a security zone in southern Lebanon extending to the Litani River. Heavy Israeli strikes hit Beirut and surrounding areas, while Hezbollah continued retaliatory fire across the border.

stories.title: Iran conflict sees controlled uncertainty as Trump mixes diplomacy with pressure - analysis
stories.summary: The Trump administration is pursuing a dual-track strategy toward Iran, combining military escalation with diplomatic engagement. This approach has created deliberate ambiguity that has helped stabilize financial markets while keeping Tehran uncertain about Washington's next steps.

stories.title: Russian drone strikes center of Ivano-Frankivsk, damaging maternity hospital
stories.summary: A Russian drone strike hit the central area of Ivano-Frankivsk in western Ukraine, damaging windows in several buildings including a maternity hospital. Ukrainian authorities reported no casualties from the attack.

stories.title: ‘Bleeding cash’: UK investment plan delay hurting key suppliers, industry groups warn
stories.summary: UK defense industry trade body ADS warned British lawmakers that delays in government investment plans are forcing small and medium enterprises out of the defense supply sector. Defense director Samira Braund said the financial strain on key suppliers is causing significant concern across the industry.

stories.title: IDF names Muhammad Ali Kourani as Quds Force member killed in Beirut strike
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces identified Muhammad Ali Kourani as an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Quds Force member killed in an Israeli airstrike in Beirut, Lebanon. The IDF confirmed the strike took place on Monday afternoon but did not initially disclose the target's identity.

stories.title: Children informing on parents, teachers beaten, collaborators later jailed — researcher details Russia’s occupation playbook
stories.summary: A researcher detailed how Russia attempted to replicate its Crimea Russification strategy in occupied parts of Zaporizhzhia and Kherson oblasts. The plan encountered unexpected local resistance, extending the process to three and a half years rather than the nine months Russia had originally projected.

stories.title: LHC sustains objection on plea against acquittal of PM Shehbaz, his sons in money laundering case
stories.summary: The Lahore High Court upheld an objection challenging the maintainability of a petition filed against the acquittal of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and his sons in a 16-billion-rupee money laundering case. Chief Justice Aalia Neelum heard the case after the registrar's office questioned the petitioner's legal standing to bring the challenge.

stories.title: Largest strike of war—Russia unleashes 948 drones in 24 hours, as spring offensive begins
stories.summary: Russia launched a record 948 drones in a single 24-hour period against Ukraine, marking the largest aerial attack of the war. The assault, which included Shahed drones and ballistic missiles, was aimed at exhausting Ukrainian air defenses as part of a broader spring offensive.

stories.title: Russia Stops Ammonium Nitrate Exports for 1 Month
stories.summary: Russia imposed a one-month halt on ammonium nitrate exports. The suspension coincides with a global supply shortage driven by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a waterway through which approximately 24% of the world's ammonia supply transits.

stories.title: Philippine President declares energy emergency over West Asia conflict risks
stories.summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. declared an energy emergency citing risks stemming from the conflict in West Asia. He announced the formation of a committee tasked with ensuring the orderly supply and distribution of fuel, food, medicines, and other essential goods.

stories.title: Russian troops drop nine aerial bombs on Druzhkivka, deaths and injuries reported
stories.summary: Russian forces dropped nine aerial bombs on Druzhkivka in Ukraine's Donetsk region on March 24. The airstrike killed at least one woman and injured several other people in the city.

stories.title: America must adopt a Sixth Domain of warfare doctrine
stories.summary: A sponsored article argues the United States should adopt a "Sixth Domain" warfare doctrine to address emerging threats from autonomous and networked systems. The concept focuses on how low-cost consumer electronics can be used to neutralize expensive conventional military platforms.

stories.title: Trump says he is 'talking to the right' people in Iran to make a deal
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated he is in negotiations with "the right people" in Iran to reach an agreement ending hostilities, though he declined to share specifics. He did not confirm whether envoy Steve Witkoff or Jared Kushner had planned talks. Pakistan has offered to host U.S.-Iran discussions.

stories.title: Airlines cancel more flights as Middle East conflict escalates
stories.summary: Airlines continued canceling flights across the Middle East as the Iran conflict escalated, causing major disruptions to global air travel. Key aviation hubs including Dubai and Doha were significantly affected by the cancellations.

stories.title: War on Iran: Why Trump blinked first
stories.summary: An analysis argues that President Trump moved toward de-escalation in the Iran conflict, prioritizing oil prices and market stability over sustained military action. The piece suggests Trump is calibrating the conflict based on economic indicators rather than strategic military objectives.

stories.title: Iran war has been winding down since mid-March after decline in bombing - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis indicates that the pace of U.S. and Israeli strikes in the Iran conflict has declined since mid-March, suggesting the war has been winding down. This trend contradicts official statements from both governments claiming maximum strike intensity is being maintained.

stories.title: Iran war puts South Asia's Gulf remittances at risk
stories.summary: Economists warn that a prolonged conflict in the Middle East could disrupt remittance flows from Gulf states to South Asia, where millions of migrant workers depend on employment in the region to send money home to their families.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia diverged with Turkey and Pakistan on condemning Iran
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia broke with Turkey and Pakistan in its response to the conflict with Iran. The three countries had been engaged in security pact discussions before the war began, but the onset of hostilities shifted Riyadh's priorities toward Tehran, creating a diplomatic divergence among the partners.

stories.title: Syrian army says base targeted by missiles from Iraq
stories.summary: A missile attack launched from Iraqi territory struck a Syrian army base in northeastern Syria, according to Syrian military officials. The strike caused damage to the facility but resulted in no reported casualties.

stories.title: Oil depot still on fire for second day following attack on Russian Primorsk port
stories.summary: An oil depot at the port of Primorsk in Russia's Leningrad region continued burning for a second consecutive day following a strike on the facility.

stories.title: Israel’s military to occupy swathe of southern Lebanon, Defence Chief says
stories.summary: Israel's defense chief announced plans for the military to occupy a swathe of southern Lebanon. Israeli strikes across southern Lebanon and parts of Beirut have caused widespread destruction and killed more than 1,000 people.

stories.title: War on Iran: 'Fought on faulty assumptions, notion of externally delivered regime change delusional'
stories.summary: Barbara Slavin, a Distinguished Fellow at the Stimson Center, argued that the war on Iran was built on faulty assumptions and lacked coherent strategy. She said diplomatic alternatives were dismissed and intelligence warnings were inadequately considered, and that military actions have strengthened Iranian hardliners and destabilized the global economy.

stories.title: Russia launches 948 drones at Ukraine in largest attack over 24-hour period
stories.summary: Russia launched 948 drones at Ukraine in what officials described as the largest attack over a 24-hour period. Cities across western Ukraine were hit, with residential buildings damaged and many people injured.

stories.title: Iran names successor to security chief killed in US-Israeli attack
stories.summary: Iran appointed Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, a former IRGC commander, as the new chief of the Supreme National Security Council. He replaces Ali Larijani, who was killed in a US-Israeli attack.

stories.title: Afghanistan frees detained US citizen Dennis Coyle as gesture of ‘goodwill’
stories.summary: Afghanistan released detained US citizen Dennis Coyle in what it described as a gesture of goodwill. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio welcomed the release as a positive step and thanked Qatar and the UAE for their assistance in securing it.

stories.title: Israeli army says strike killed Lebanese member of Quds Force
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it killed a Lebanese member of Iran's Quds Force in a strike near Beirut. The target was described as a Hezbollah-linked figure, and the strike hit an upscale suburb of the Lebanese capital.

stories.title: Trump’s approval hits new 36% low as fuel prices surge amid Iran war, poll finds
stories.summary: A Reuters/Ipsos poll found US President Donald Trump's approval rating dropped to 36 percent, its lowest since his return to office. The decline was driven by surging fuel prices and widespread disapproval of the war on Iran, down from 40 percent the previous week.

stories.title: Israeli strike lands near Roman ruins in Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli strike hit a building in the Lebanese city of Tyre, landing near the city's ancient Roman ruins. Smoke was seen rising close to the archaeological site following the strike.

stories.title: Lebanon's humanitarian crisis worsens as fighting continues
stories.summary: The humanitarian crisis in Lebanon is worsening as fighting between Israel and Hezbollah continues, with hundreds of thousands of Lebanese civilians displaced. Israel has announced it may occupy southern Lebanon on a long-term basis.

stories.title: Arabic-language Wikipedia filled with terrorist propaganda, bias – report
stories.summary: A report by the World Jewish Congress found that Arabic-language Wikipedia articles on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict contained significant bias, with up to 50 percent of citations in some entries sourced from material produced by Hamas, Hezbollah, and other designated groups.

stories.title: Kim Jong Un says North Korea will never give up on nuclear weapons
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un declared that North Korea will never abandon its pursuit of nuclear weapons.

stories.title: The War in Iran and Implications for the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Regime
stories.summary: The article examines how Iran's nuclear activities have posed a major challenge to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) framework. Iran, an NPT signatory, has maintained its nuclear program is peaceful, but its activities prompted international diplomatic, economic, and covert efforts to constrain its progress.

stories.title: War update: Defense Forces repel 17 Russian assaults in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces repelled 17 Russian assaults in the Pokrovsk sector as of the afternoon update. A total of 49 enemy attacks were recorded along the front line, with the most intense fighting occurring in the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors.

stories.title: Anthropic challenges US Pentagon’s ban in San Francisco court showdown
stories.summary: Anthropic, the AI company, has filed a legal challenge against the U.S. Pentagon in a San Francisco court. The company accuses the Department of Defense of unlawful retaliation after Anthropic refused to loosen its AI safety restrictions for military applications.

stories.title: Israel steps up assassinations in Gaza despite 'ceasefire'
stories.summary: Israeli forces have increased targeted killings of Hamas officials in Gaza despite an ostensible ceasefire. The escalation reportedly comes as international attention has shifted from Gaza toward the conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Death of ATV driver unleashes new outburst of settler attacks on Palestinians
stories.summary: Following the death of ATV driver Yehuda Sherman in a suspected ramming attack, Israeli settlers launched a wave of violent assaults against Palestinians across the occupied West Bank. Reports indicate authorities have largely failed to intervene as the attacks intensified an already rising climate of fear.

stories.title: US to send 3,000 airborne soldiers to Middle East
stories.summary: The Pentagon plans to deploy approximately 3,000 soldiers from the 82nd Airborne Division to the Middle East to support operations against Iran, according to U.S. officials cited by The Wall Street Journal. A written deployment order is expected imminently, though the specific destination and timeline have not been disclosed.

stories.title: Lebanon withdraws accreditation of Iran’s Ambassador, orders him to leave country
stories.summary: Lebanon has withdrawn the accreditation of Iran's ambassador and ordered him to leave the country. A Foreign Ministry spokesperson confirmed that Iran's embassy will continue to operate under a Chargé d'Affaires to head its diplomatic mission in Beirut.

stories.title: Israeli soldiers accused of ‘torturing’ toddler in Gaza
stories.summary: The family of a two-year-old boy in Gaza has accused Israeli soldiers of torturing the toddler in an effort to extract information about his father. The allegations concern actions taken by Israeli forces operating within the Gaza Strip.

stories.title: Israel moves to advance death penalty law targeting Palestinians
stories.summary: Israel's parliament is advancing legislation that would allow the death penalty for Palestinian prisoners convicted of terrorism-related offenses. The proposed law would specifically exempt Jewish Israeli citizens from the provision.

stories.title: Bill Cosby ordered to pay $19.25m to woman in decades-old assault case
stories.summary: A California court ordered actor Bill Cosby to pay $19.25 million in damages to a woman who accused him of drugging and sexually assaulting her in the early 1970s.

stories.title: French economic growth undercut by war in Iran, national statistics office says
stories.summary: France's Insee national statistics agency reported that the economy will grow only 0.2% in the first half of the year, down from the previously forecast 0.3%, due to higher inflation linked to the war in Iran. Inflation is expected to exceed 2% in coming months, up sharply from 1.1% in February.

stories.title: Russians strike residential building in Lviv with drone
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a residential building on Chervonoi Kalyny Avenue in Lviv, western Ukraine, using a drone. The attack targeted civilian infrastructure in a city far from the front lines.

stories.title: French authorities search Paris arm of Swiss bank in Epstein-linked probe
stories.summary: French financial prosecutors conducted searches at several locations in Paris, including the local branch of Swiss private bank Edmond de Rothschild, as part of a probe linked to the Jeffrey Epstein files. The investigation, opened last month, focuses on suspicions of bribery involving a foreign public official and complicity.

stories.title: PSX rallies 1,200 points after Eid break
stories.summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange's KSE-100 index rose 1,225.99 points, or 0.80%, to close at 153,966.36 following the Eid holiday break. The rally was driven by positive cues from international markets, easing geopolitical tensions, and declining global oil prices.

stories.title: The Iran War Is Coming for Your Grocery Bill
stories.summary: The article highlights how the ongoing war in Iran is expected to drive up consumer prices beyond fuel costs, affecting grocery bills. Rising energy and supply-chain disruptions linked to the conflict are anticipated to increase food prices for American consumers.

stories.title: State Duma Passes Bill Criminalizing Denial of ‘Soviet Genocide’
stories.summary: Russia's State Duma passed legislation that would criminalize the denial of genocide committed against Soviet citizens during World War II. The bill broadly defines the offense to cover any denial that such a genocide took place.

stories.title: Trump's approval hits new 36 percent low, Reuters-Ipsos poll finds
stories.summary: A Reuters-Ipsos poll found U.S. President Donald Trump's approval rating dropped to 36 percent, its lowest since he returned to office. The decline followed rising fuel prices and widespread disapproval of the military campaign he launched against Iran on February 28.

stories.title: OGDCL commences oil production from development well in Hyderabad
stories.summary: Pakistan's Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL) began oil production from its Pasakhi-13 development well in Hyderabad, producing 460 barrels per day. The well represents Pakistan's first successful horizontal oil well in a clastic reservoir, drilled to a measured depth of 2,966 metres.

stories.title: University in occupied Kashmir recommends dropping Jinnah, Muslim thinkers from syllabus after student protests
stories.summary: A panel at the University of Jammu in India-administered Kashmir recommended removing topics on Muhammad Ali Jinnah, Allama Iqbal, and Syed Ahmad Khan from its MA Political Science syllabus. The recommendation followed campus protests by the ABVP, the student wing of India's ruling party-affiliated Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh.

stories.title: Palestinian FA urges Israel ban over FIFA discrimination report
stories.summary: The Palestinian Football Association called on FIFA to ban Israel from international football competitions. The push cites allegations of racism and findings from a FIFA discrimination report against the Israeli Football Association.

stories.title: Everyday life in Asia is being upended by Iran war fuel crisis
stories.summary: Rising oil and gas prices stemming from the Iran conflict are disrupting daily life across Asia. The region's heavy dependence on Gulf energy supplies has left it vulnerable to shortages caused by the war.

stories.title: Is Iran's parliamentary speaker Ghalibaf negotiating with the US?
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump claimed the United States had been in negotiations with an unnamed senior Iranian leader. Media reports speculated the interlocutor may be Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, a 64-year-old former pilot.

stories.title: Evidence shows Israeli 'double tap' attack killed Hind Rajab
stories.summary: Campaign group Avaaz released a report presenting what it called substantial evidence that the Israeli military carried out a double-tap strike that killed five-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab. A double-tap attack involves a second strike on the same location shortly after the first.

stories.title: Oil refinery explosion reported in Texas
stories.summary: An explosion occurred at Valero's Port Arthur Refinery in Texas, prompting local officials to issue a shelter-in-place order for nearby residents. Media reports showed large flames and black smoke rising from the facility.

stories.title: 3 injured as fragments of Iranian missile fall in unrecognized Bedouin village
stories.summary: Fragments of an Iranian missile struck an unrecognized Bedouin village in Israel, injuring three people. A man was seriously wounded, while his wife and two-month-old baby sustained light injuries. Most residents of the community lack access to bomb shelters.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war Highlights: Trump says Iran 'wants to make a deal', but Islamic Republic denies any talks
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated that Iran "wants to make a deal," but Iranian officials denied any negotiations were taking place. Oil prices fell and stock markets rose as observers tried to interpret the conflicting signals.

stories.title: Ghana, European Union agree defence pact
stories.summary: Ghana and the European Union signed a defence cooperation pact in Accra. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas and Ghanaian Vice President Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang signed the agreement, which covers counterterrorism, intelligence sharing, and crisis response.

stories.title: Ashab al-Yamin: The obscure new group claiming Jewish ambulance attack
stories.summary: A previously unknown group called Ashab al-Yamin claimed responsibility for an arson attack on ambulances owned by a Jewish charity in the Golders Green area of north London. London's Metropolitan Police said it was too early to attribute the attack to Iran.

stories.title: Israel says it will take control of large buffer zone in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel announced it would take control of a large buffer zone in southern Lebanon. Defence officials stated that thousands of displaced Lebanese residents would not be permitted to return to their homes until northern Israel is deemed safe.

stories.title: United States: ICE agents patrol airports amid govt shutdown
stories.summary: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents began deploying to major airports amid a prolonged partial government shutdown. The move placed ICE personnel in highly visible roles at crowded transport hubs as officials sought to address growing travel disruptions.

stories.title: Pete said, ‘Let’s do it’: Trump on decision-making over Iran attack
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump referenced advisor Pete in describing the decision-making process behind a military strike on Iran. He also disclosed that the U.S. and Iran have held what he called productive conversations aimed at a complete resolution of the broader conflict in West Asia.

stories.title: TKMS and ST Engineering to create submarine service ‘hub’ in Singapore
stories.summary: German shipbuilder TKMS and Singapore's ST Engineering announced plans to establish a submarine maintenance hub in Singapore. The facility would service both Singaporean and international TKMS submarines transiting the region.

stories.title: 4 dead as Russia fires nearly 400 drones at Ukraine with signs spring offensive has begun
stories.summary: Russia launched nearly 400 long-range drones at Ukraine in its largest such attack in weeks, striking civilian areas including the capital Kyiv. At least four people were killed and 35 injured. Moscow simultaneously intensified ground operations along the front lines in what may signal the start of a spring offensive.

stories.title: NASA plans moon base instead of orbital lunar station
stories.summary: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman announced the agency will shift from building an orbiting lunar station to constructing a base on the moon's surface. The decision comes as the United States competes with Russia and China in a renewed race to establish a presence on the moon.

stories.title: Ghana and EU sign landmark defence deal to combat militant Islamist threat
stories.summary: Ghana signed a defense agreement with the European Union aimed at countering militant Islamist threats. Ghana's vice-president noted the country is the first in Africa to conclude such a deal with the EU.

stories.title: Kratos scores $447M Space Force award for missile tracking ground system
stories.summary: Kratos Defense & Security Solutions received a $447 million contract from the U.S. Space Force for a missile tracking ground system. The award follows an earlier Space Force contract with Parsons for the Resilient Missile Warning Tracking medium Earth orbit satellite program's ground operations center.

stories.title: Tension rises between Israel and Lebanon as IDF occupies south of Litani river
stories.summary: Israel announced on March 24 that its military would seize control of southern Lebanon up to the Litani River. The ongoing campaign has killed at least 1,039 people and displaced over a million during more than three weeks of fighting with Hezbollah. The Iran-backed group has vowed to resist.

stories.title: Iran strikes put in question US-Israeli attacks's impact on military capabilities
stories.summary: Iranian drone strikes hit Tel Aviv, damaging residential buildings and injuring several people. The attacks raised questions about whether prior U.S.-Israeli strikes had significantly degraded Iran's military capabilities. Analysts noted Iran has launched sporadic strikes apparently aimed at preserving its arsenal.

stories.title: Kenya fuel retailers running short of supplies amid Middle East war
stories.summary: Hundreds of fuel retailers across Kenya are experiencing supply shortages linked to the ongoing war in the Middle East. The head of the Petroleum Outlets Association of Kenya attributed the disruptions to conflict-related impacts on global fuel supply chains.

stories.title: Hezbollah calls on Lebanon to 'immediately reverse' expulsion of Iranian ambassador
stories.summary: Hezbollah demanded that Lebanon immediately reverse its decision to expel Iran's ambassador, calling the move a "sin." Lebanon's foreign ministry had withdrawn the accreditation of the Iranian ambassador on Tuesday and given him until Sunday to leave the country.

stories.title: UK’s King Charles will be patron for major Jewish security organization
stories.summary: King Charles III will serve as patron of the Community Security Trust, a major organization advising Britain's estimated 280,000 Jews on security matters. The announcement came one day after an arson attack in London targeted ambulances belonging to a Jewish group.

stories.title: Gaza Boxing Women: Punching through war, trauma and displacement
stories.summary: In Gaza, girls and young women have been rebuilding a boxing community amid ongoing conflict and displacement. Participants use the sport to cope with grief and trauma while challenging social norms.

stories.title: Israel announces territorial seizure in Lebanon up to Litani River
stories.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Katz announced that Israeli forces would control remaining bridges and a security zone up to the Litani River in southern Lebanon. The directive was issued during a meeting with the military chief of staff.

stories.title: Man convicted of hate crime for attacking Israeli in New York after Oct. 7
stories.summary: Yehia Amin was convicted of a hate crime in New York for punching an Israeli tourist following the October 7 attacks and sentenced to 90 days in prison. Separately, a vandal who defaced the home of the Brooklyn Museum's Jewish director had a felony charge dropped.

stories.title: CERT warns ‘hostile actors’ could exploit supply chains to target national infrastructure
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Computer Emergency Response Team issued a cybersecurity advisory warning that hostile actors may exploit supply chain vulnerabilities to target critical national infrastructure, including power grids, banking systems, and defense networks. The advisory noted that even minor lapses in hardware and software delivery could trigger large-scale failures.

stories.title: Iran parliament speaker: ‘No negotiations with the US’
stories.summary: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf stated on Monday that Iran is not engaged in negotiations with the United States to end the ongoing war.

stories.title: Israeli hitmakers launch unexpected global chart topper
stories.summary: Israeli music group Temper City released their debut single 'Self Aware,' which reached number one on both TikTok and Spotify's global viral charts.

stories.title: At Least 1 Killed in Apartment Explosion in Annexed Crimea
stories.summary: At least one person was killed in an explosion at an apartment building in Russian-annexed Crimea. Investigators are working to determine the cause but have ruled out a gas leak.

stories.title: Top official says US still assessing how to test nuclear weapons
stories.summary: US Undersecretary of State Thomas DiNanno told a Senate committee that the administration is still assessing how to carry out President Donald Trump's order to resume nuclear weapons testing. He said no discussions have taken place regarding atmospheric nuclear tests.

stories.title: Woman shot dead in Galilee, taking 2026 toll in Arab community to 74
stories.summary: A woman, approximately 35 years old, was shot and killed in an agricultural area in the town of Reineh in the Galilee region. Her death brings the 2026 homicide toll in Israel's Arab community to 74 and marks the fifth female homicide victim this year amid ongoing organized crime violence.

stories.title: Who wins what in the EU's new trade deal with Australia?
stories.summary: The European Union and Australia have finalized a long-delayed free trade agreement. The deal comes as both parties face pressure from US tariffs and Chinese industrial competition, prompting them to resolve previous trade disputes.

stories.title: 'I intend to go back to my country': Exiled Ugandan opposition leader Bobi Wine
stories.summary: Exiled Ugandan opposition leader Bobi Wine told FRANCE 24 that he intends to return to Uganda after resurfacing in Washington following nearly two months in hiding. Wine said he remains under threat and called for international sanctions against President Yoweri Museveni and his son.

stories.title: Why is Pakistan being touted as mediator between US and Iran?
stories.summary: Pakistan is positioning itself as a potential mediator between the United States and Iran should either side agree to engage in talks aimed at resolving their conflict.

stories.title: Iranian missile intercepted over Lebanese airspace: Report
stories.summary: An Iranian missile was intercepted over Lebanese airspace for the first time on Tuesday, according to three senior Lebanese security sources. Two sources said a foreign naval vessel carried out the interception. Shrapnel reportedly fell over towns north of Beirut, causing light injuries.

stories.title: Israel prepares to mobilise 400,000 reservists in Lebanon war
stories.summary: Israel is preparing to mobilize up to 400,000 military reservists as it escalates operations against Lebanon. Deadly airstrikes have intensified even as ground advances remain limited.

stories.title: Bradley replacement is still on track, says Army acquisitions boss
stories.summary: The US Army's acquisitions chief confirmed that the program to replace the Bradley infantry fighting vehicle remains on schedule. The update came one year into the Army Transformation Initiative, which also includes a drone marketplace and other modernization efforts.

stories.title: North Korea’s Kim vows ‘irreversible’ nuclear status, warns Seoul of ‘merciless’ response
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un declared that the country's nuclear-armed status is irreversible and will never be relinquished. In a policy address to the Supreme People's Assembly, Kim said South Korea would soon be designated the "most hostile state" and accused the United States of committing "state terrorism."

stories.title: War as a Force of Destruction, Change, and Opportunity
stories.summary: The Ukraine Compass, a weekly digest published by War on the Rocks, curates Ukrainian media commentary and analysis on the war and its effects. The series aims to present how Ukrainians themselves debate issues of politics, daily life, and public discourse during the conflict.

stories.title: Iran arrests 466 people accused of online activity undermining national security: report
stories.summary: Iranian authorities arrested 466 people accused of online activity deemed a threat to national security. Iranian media reported over 1,000 total arrests in the past month, targeting individuals accused of filming sensitive locations, sharing anti-government content, or cooperating with foreign adversaries.

stories.title: Bangladesh's influential former army general arrested
stories.summary: Bangladeshi police in plain clothes arrested retired Lieutenant General Masud Uddin Chowdhury. He was a key figure in the 2007 government change that installed an interim administration, which governed Bangladesh until elections were held in 2008.

stories.title: North Korea head uses US 'aggression' to justify nuclear arsenal
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has cited what he describes as US and Israeli aggression in the region to justify his country's nuclear weapons program. Kim has also publicly spoken out against the ongoing war involving Iran.

stories.title: Central Africa: UAE and CEMAC - A Gradually Expanding Economic Partnership
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates is gradually expanding its economic partnership with the Central African Economic and Monetary Community (CEMAC), a bloc traditionally aligned with France, China, the United States, and the European Union. Shifts in the global political economy are enabling emerging actors like the UAE to increase their presence across Central Africa in areas such as infrastructure, finance, and trade.

stories.title: Hong Kong to meet uncertainty with openness, John Lee tells Boao Forum for Asia
stories.summary: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee Ka-chiu addressed the Boao Forum for Asia in Hainan, pledging that Hong Kong would respond to rising geopolitical tensions with openness rather than isolation. Lee called on economies to unite in promoting free trade and praised China's commitment to multilateral trade.

stories.title: China alleges Tokyo embassy break-in, protests to Japan
stories.summary: China has formally protested to Japan over an alleged break-in at its embassy in Tokyo. A Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said Beijing was "deeply shocked" by the incident and urged Japan to conduct a thorough investigation, punish those responsible, and provide an explanation.

stories.title: Sadapay says app unavailable after Amazon Web Services disrupted in Bahrain amid war on Iran
stories.summary: Pakistani fintech company Sadapay reported that its mobile application became unavailable to all users after Amazon Web Services infrastructure in Bahrain was disrupted. The company attributed the outage to the impact of the US-Israel conflict with Iran, which has affected services and infrastructure in Gulf countries including Bahrain.
